name: Maipo Valley
shape: Chile Decreto 464, drawn from its comunas and provinces
keyfacts: Under Chile's official zoning, Pirque, Puente Alto and Buin may use the Andes term, while Isla de Maipo, Talagante and Melipilla may use Entre Cordilleras.
Its eastern vineyards lie in the Andes foothills, and its western vineyards reach the sandy soils of the Coastal Range.
Cabernet Sauvignon is the main variety, and Merlot, Syrah and Carmenère also thrive here.
The valley lies across the Andes from Mendoza Province.

notes: Maipo Cabernet Sauvignon is marked by pervasive blackcurrant fruit and an earthy, dusty note.

blurb.text: A subregion of the Central Valley, in the Metropolitana area, split into Alto, Central and Pacific Maipo. Cabernet Sauvignon covers 52 percent of its vines, well ahead of Merlot, Syrah, Carmenère, Sauvignon Blanc and Chardonnay.
